name: Africa, Middle East & South Asia
summary: PepsiCo AMESA sector covering India, Pakistan, the Middle East, and Sub-Saharan Africa. Combined Foods and Beverages business. Kurkure, Lay's India, 7UP, and PepsiCo's AMESA portfolio.
toneOfVoice: Respectful, precise, culturally aware. AMESA content spans many languages and religious traditions — content must be inclusive of that diversity by default. Prefer neutral, formal register in employee-facing content; casual tone is a market-level choice, not a sector default.
contentStrategy: AMESA is highly diverse — Hindi, Urdu, Arabic, Bengali, English, and multiple African languages all appear across markets. Prioritize: (1) content that respects religious observances (Ramadan, festival calendars, halal certification for beverages and foods); (2) agriculture and supply-chain content given the sector's manufacturing and sourcing footprint; (3) local brand-specific content (Kurkure, Lehar, Aliva, Lay's India variants); (4) manufacturing safety and community programs that resonate across the sector.
contentGuidelines: 1. When calendars are referenced, include local + Gregorian dates where practical. 2. Halal certification and food handling must be called out explicitly for beverage and food content in Muslim-majority markets. 3. Reference AMESA-specific brands (Kurkure, Lehar, Aliva, Lay's India, 7UP MENA) alongside global brands. 4. Respect gender-neutral language conventions in each market's dominant language. 5. Cross-country programs (Positive Agriculture, PepsiCo Foundation initiatives) should identify which countries the program operates in.
regulatoryNotes: Food safety: FSSAI (India), SFDA (Saudi Arabia), various regional standards. Halal certification requirements vary by market and by product category. India-specific: labor laws under the Code on Wages and the Industrial Relations Code; state-level variations. Middle East: labor laws differ significantly by GCC country. Nutrition and health claims subject to local advertising standards (ASCI in India, GCC Standardization Organization).
seoNotes: AMESA content ranks across many languages. English is the shared working language for internal content but market-level translation is critical. Include local brand names (Kurkure, Lehar) and program names in the local language when relevant.
